Resolves #19829

A `wrapText` tree column now wraps its labels in a content-sized grid, and its rows grow to fit them. In a fixed-height grid the label keeps its one-line ellipsis.

- **Measured element:** the tree cell exposes its label's vdom (`textVdom`). `View#measureRowHeights` measures it as it measures a text cell's `.neo-grid-cell-text`, and reads padding and borders per column, because a helper-lines tree cell has no vertical padding.
- **Helper lines:** only the label wraps. The indent and the toggle keep spanning the row, so the lines stay unbroken when another column is taller.
- **Wrap switch:** the tree column's `cellCls` marks a cell `neo-wrap-text` in content-sized grids. Cell classes render on every pass, so switching `contentSizedRows` or `wrapText` reaches the cells of unchanged records, and the cell component holds no wrap state.
- **Hidden projection:** it keeps measuring declared text only. A component column, one that declares `cellDepth`, is never rendered there. A font change in a grid with no such text columns re-measures the rows where they show.
- **Shown-cell fence:** `View#isShown` gets a component arm. A component cell counts as shown once its last landed update rendered its root's classes and style, and its label, as its vdom describes them. Its `needsVdomUpdate` cannot tell: a row's update carries a cell component's vdom without clearing the flag, so after a filter every re-bound tree cell stayed flagged and unmeasured.
- **Trigger:** a tree cell's own landed update schedules the view's measure pass.
- **Release note:** the 13.3.0 note's content-sized section now covers tree columns. Its bounds no longer list tree stores as deferred; only measuring tree labels ahead of the scroll is.

Evidence: L2 (unit arms on the measurement, each red under its mutation) + L3 (e2e on a real tree grid, with the browser's layout as the oracle).

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | e2e `TreeContentSized.spec.mjs` › a long tree label wraps, and its row grows to fit it |
| AC-2 | e2e › expand, collapse and re-expand keep every row fitted and stacked |
| AC-3 | e2e › a fixed-height grid keeps the tree label on one line with an ellipsis |
| AC-4 | unit `WrapTextMeasure.spec.mjs` › tree cells: measured through the label; a re-bound cell is not read before its own update lands, with a new label or the same label one level deeper; wrap switches reach unchanged records; a font change keeps the labels measurable; hidden premeasurement constructs no tree cells |
| AC-5 | e2e › the tree column's header filter keeps the matches with their ancestors, and the rows refit. Unit › a filter that shows other records re-binds the tree cells, and their rows fit the new labels |

## Deltas from ticket
- The ticket's first draft wrapped the whole cell component in the measured block. That breaks the helper lines wherever another column is taller, so the component names its label instead; the ticket's Fix is revised to match.

## Test Evidence
- Red first: the wrap tests failed on dev's code ("the tree label is cut off"). The header filter test then failed against the first fence, which read the cell component's `needsVdomUpdate` ("Container.mjs: height 32, its text needs 115").
- Mutations, each reverted before the commit:
  - without the label compare, two arms go red;
  - without the root style compare, the deeper-label arm;
  - without the hook, the re-bind arm;
  - with the flag check added back, the filter arm.
- Review round 1 (Emmy): the three new arms were red on `8daf937f61`:
  - wrapping survived `contentSizedRows` off;
  - hidden passes took the tree instances from 15 to 54;
  - after a font change, a label measured 45 instead of 65.

  They pass at `8243cc0594`. Each guard reds its arm under mutation.
- `test/playwright/unit/grid/`: 321 passed. `test/playwright/e2e/grid/`: 195 passed at `8243cc0594` (the NL specs need a Brain runtime root and were not selected).
- Screenshot of the fixture: the wrapped label grows its row, and the helper lines run unbroken through the tall rows.

- [ ] None beyond CI: the e2e drives a real tree grid in Chromium.
